name: Thornwake Glade
descriptionSeed: Deep in the wilds where the interference thins, a grove that the transition changed rather than broke — old trees grown strange and deliberate, clearings that seem arranged, animals that watch too knowingly. Something tends this place. The few who live at its edge call themselves wardens and won't say to whom. For an ENT or a Beastfriend the Glade reads almost as home; for anyone else it's beautiful and quietly conditional — welcome is extended, and watched. No river-plot reaches here; the Glade's concerns are older and greener.
encounterFlavor: A living quiet that pays attention. Beasts that parley if you know how; wardens who test your intent before your skill; the grove itself adjusting to whether you take or tend.
questSeeds: Warden Isolde tends the Glade for something she'll only call 'the Green Accord,' and it is failing — the grove is dreaming badly, and she needs someone who can walk the wilds to find why
A foundling child, Burr, was left at the Glade's edge and the grove has half-adopted them; the wardens disagree bitterly about whether to raise a human here or return them to people
Poachers from the Disputed Zone are taking Glade-touched beasts to sell as curiosities; stopping them cleanly matters, because the Glade remembers who spills blood in it
The Old Stag — something between an animal and a presence — is dying, and what happens to the Green Accord when it does is a question the wardens are terrified to answer

worldPosNote: Near-centre folk country — the Valley sits where all axes cross faintly, so longitude spreads and colatitude stays low. (SNG-180: authored position — WHERE it sits. Independent of axisVector, which is WHAT it is; a bastion is where the two disagree.)
_regionSplit: ⛔ SNG-387: was `valley`. The valley spanned 90 WALKING DAYS — 30% of the way round the world — with a 53° longitude gap splitting it cleanly in two. ⚠️ These six say what they are in their own descriptions: 'where the sonic civilization meets the valley floor', 'the rim of the Radiant Plateau', 'built on stilts by people who wanted out from under BOTH CITIES'. This is not the Valley. It is the country BETWEEN the two craft-family civilisations, and being between them is its whole identity. Erik: 'the Valley is not the whole world.'
appearance: A grove of old trees grown into deliberate arrangements — trunks curving to frame gaps, clearings that read as rooms with entrances. Thorn thickets forming walls. Green light, deep leaf-litter, and nothing quite random.

_retiredAxes_20260919._why: ⛔ SNG-633 — TWO AXES RETIRED, AND NOT MAPPED ONTO ANOTHER. `individual_collective` and `tradition_innovation` were authored on 33 records and existed nowhere else: not in `world_node_atlas.axisOrder`, which is TWELVE ORDERED SLOTS and the thing `axisVector` is derived from on every location; not in the GM prompt; and with zero readers in the engine. ⚠️ Erik: 'I don't recall intentionally making these axes — it likely happened along the way. I'm worried about losing coherence.' He was right and I was wrong: I argued to ADD them because they describe real territory, and the twelve is a GEOMETRY rather than a count — a thirteenth means widening a twelve-slot vector on 143 locations and changing a build-time seam. ⛑ AND I DID NOT FOLD THEM INTO A NEIGHBOURING AXIS, because most of these records ALREADY CARRY the nearest candidate with a different authored value — Kestrel's Roost has its own `chaos_order`, and merging would have overwritten a real number with a guess. **The values are preserved below rather than converted, so nothing is lost if they are ever made real.**
